plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $7, I will bid exactly $7 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying only that second-highest bid, and never overpay. Bidding above value risks winning at a price above your value (loss), while bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single-round game with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my value of $32 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay only the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. This means there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down - overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $15, I should bid exactly $15 to maximize expected profit regardless of what the other bidders do.
